name: PayPal
notes: PayPal's hosted MCP is built for merchants (invoices, orders, disputes, subscriptions, shipment tracking, transaction reporting) and, like the REST API, needs a PayPal Business account in production, so a personal account cannot use it. For a personal account the route is the account's activity download (transaction history) in PayPal's settings. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256.

name: Todoist
notes: Doist hosts the official Todoist MCP server, listed in the registry as net.todoist/mcp; sign-in runs on todoist.com and the API is free, with some features limited by the person's plan. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256, token auth none or client secret.

name: Evernote
notes: Evernote's own remote MCP server signs in with OAuth and dynamic client registration and works on paid personal, Business and Teams plans, not free Basic; it is an open beta with no waitlist or access request, though Evernote says it 'is rolling out gradually' and ineligible accounts see a message when connecting. The legacy API is deprecated. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256, public clients (auth method none); Registry 2026-10-08: only a community entry (github.com/verygoodplugins/mcp-evernote).

name: Robinhood
notes: Robinhood's own Trading MCP (US only) lets an agent read the person's Robinhood accounts and trade only in a separate Agentic account the person opens and funds; Robinhood names "any localhost platform" as a supported client and charges no extra fee. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, token auth none; registry entries named Robinhood are community (e.g. io.github.verygoodplugins/robinhood-mcp).

name: Philips Hue
notes: Signify runs a remote MCP on its meethue.com domain with open dynamic client registration, but no Hue developer or support page documents it yet, so tools and stability are unconfirmed; the documented routes are the local Bridge API and the Remote Hue API (free developer account). Community servers exist (e.g. github.com/m2ai-mcp-servers/mcp-philips-hue). Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256, token endpoint auth none.

name: Substack
notes: Substack's official MCP is read-only publication analytics (subscribers, post performance, revenue, retention) and works only for an admin of a Bestseller publication; it cannot read the person's reading list, Notes or profile, so readers get nothing from it. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256, token auth none or client_secret_basic, authorization server substack.com, scopes mcp:read and mcp.user.read.

name: TickTick
notes: TickTick documents its own Streamable HTTP MCP at mcp.ticktick.com with OAuth or a personal API token, and Claude's directory lists it. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256 (plain also offered), token auth none or client_secret_basic, authorization on ticktick.com, scopes tasks:read and tasks:write.

name: Adobe Acrobat
notes: Adobe runs an Acrobat MCP endpoint on adobe.io and brings Acrobat tools to Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini through its own connectors (free Adobe account or guest); Adobe's help pages blocked fetching, so whether any client may register and how long sessions last is unconfirmed. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, token auth none only, authorization_code grant only (no refresh token advertised).

name: Any.do
notes: Any.do's own help centre documents a free remote MCP server at https://mcp.any.do/sse (beta, all users) for tasks, reminders, workspaces and calendar; it is not in the MCP Registry. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256, token auth none allowed; the protected resource metadata sits at the /sse-suffixed path.

name: Adobe Lightroom
notes: Adobe announced its hosted Adobe for creativity MCP with Lightroom, Photoshop and other tools (shown in Claude; other clients not mentioned); a free Adobe account works, with higher limits on paid plans. Discovery 2026-10-08: auth server ims-na1.adobelogin.com, DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, client-secret token auth; scopes cover llm.assets only, so the person's Lightroom cloud library still needs the entitled-partner Lightroom API. Registry 2026-10-08: only community Adobe servers.

name: Webull
notes: Webull Cloud MCP is a vendor-hosted server where the person signs in with OAuth and picks which accounts and capabilities to grant; orders become instructions the person confirms, and Webull documents use from Codex and other clients, not only its listed assistants. Discovery 2026-10-09: protected-resource metadata at the root and path-suffixed URLs, authorization server api.webull.com, DCR yes, CIMD no, token auth none, S256.

name: Shop
notes: Shopify hosts an official Shop MCP server (catalog search, carts, Shop Pay checkout, order tracking); search works anonymously and signing in adds addresses, orders and purchase approvals. Discovery 2026-10-08 on accounts.shop.app: no DCR, CIMD yes, S256, public clients allowed; Shop now also brands its site as shop.com; not in the MCP Registry.

name: TradingView
notes: TradingView's official MCP Server (beta) documents one URL for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and any MCP client with OAuth 2.1 sign-in; it covers watchlists (read and write), market data, screener, news, fundamentals, calendars and alerts, needs an Essential or higher plan (trials excluded) and is limited to about 100 tool calls per minute. Discovery 2026-10-09: protected-resource metadata only at the path-suffixed URL (root returns 404), authorization server www.tradingview.com, DCR yes, CIMD no, S256.

name: Upwork
notes: Upwork's official remote MCP (registry com.upwork.mcp/upwork-mcp, listed in Anthropic's directory) covers job search, proposals, messages, contracts and dashboards for freelancers and clients; upwork.com docs and help pages were blocked by a Cloudflare challenge, so the client list and pricing come from the directory and registry. Discovery 2026-10-09: authorization server mcp.upwork.com advertises CIMD yes and a registration_endpoint that points at the www.upwork.com/register sign-up page (DCR unconfirmed), S256.

name: Binance
notes: Binance's official remote MCP (Agent OS) signs the person in on binance.com and trades only in a dedicated Agentic sub-account with no withdrawal scope; its docs list named clients, so acceptance of other CIMD clients is unverified. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR no, CIMD yes, S256 (protected-resource metadata only at the root path; token auth none). Not in the MCP Registry under a Binance namespace.

name: KakaoTalk
notes: Kakao runs the PlayMCP gateway, which serves the MCP servers the person adds to their PlayMCP toolbox (max 10), including Kakao's own KakaoTalk My Chatroom (send to me) server; it does not read the person's chats, and toolbox servers from third-party developers would see the data sent to them (flag). Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256; token endpoint advertises only client-secret and key methods.

name: Fastmail
notes: Fastmail's MCP server works with any MCP client that supports remote servers and covers mail, contacts and calendars with read, write and send levels chosen at sign-in (no attachments yet); API tokens also work. OAuth clients for Fastmail's other APIs are registered manually, but the MCP authorization server takes dynamic registration. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256, public clients (token auth none).

name: Home Assistant
notes: Home Assistant's built-in Model Context Protocol Server integration serves Streamable HTTP at /api/mcp on the person's own instance (template URL), exposing the Assist API and only the entities the person exposes; an administrator account is required by default. Its IndieAuth OAuth uses the client's base URL as client ID, and the docs state client_id_metadata_document_supported true and no RFC 7591 registration endpoint; remote access needs Home Assistant Cloud (paid) or a tunnel, while Kipster on the same network can reach it directly. Discovery 2026-10-09: per-instance metadata not readable without an instance; docs state CIMD yes, DCR no. Registry servers (e.g. io.github.homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp) are community projects.

name: CamScanner
notes: Official remote MCP (Streamable HTTP) signs in to the person's CamScanner account with browser OAuth, scope mcp:tools, and includes cloud document tools; not listed in the MCP Registry. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256, public client (token auth none); pricing or premium limits per tool are not documented.

name: Readwise
notes: Readwise hosts a remote MCP server signed in with the person's Readwise account; Readwise itself is a paid subscription after a 30-day trial (Reader needs the Full plan). Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes (https://readwise.io/o/register/), CIMD not advertised, S256, token auth none allowed. Registry 2026-10-08: no entry.

name: Kahoot!
notes: Kahoot documents its own MCP server for creating and editing kahoots in the person's account (no reports or game data yet). Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256; token endpoint advertises client_secret_post only.

name: Structured
notes: Structured runs an official remote MCP server (announced June 2026) for its daily planner, listing ChatGPT, Claude and other MCP clients; sign-in runs on Structured's Supabase auth server. Recurring tasks need Structured Pro. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256 (also plain).

name: Sonos
notes: Sonos 27mcp is Sonos's official remote MCP server (34 playback, volume, grouping and favorites tools, US English); Sonos says any MCP client can register it by URL. Registry entry dev.zonefoundry/sonos is a third-party relay, not Sonos. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256.

name: ClassDojo
notes: ClassDojo hosts its own MCP server and says to sign in with a ClassDojo account; scopes cover classroom read/write and messages read. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256, public clients.

name: Vimeo
notes: Vimeo hosts its own remote MCP (public beta, no access request) with scopes for public and private videos, stats, upload and edit; it needs a Vimeo Pro plan or above. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256, public clients allowed. Registry Vimeo entries are third-party gateways (e.g. pipeworx-io).

name: Swiggy
notes: Swiggy's official MCP servers (Food at /food, Instamart at /im, Dineout at /dineout) search, build carts and place cash-on-delivery orders for Swiggy accounts in India; redirect URIs are allowlisted but include http://localhost and 127.0.0.1, so a local Kipster can sign in. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256.

name: Public

name: Interactive Brokers
notes: Interactive Brokers documents a public MCP URL for any MCP client; one account per authorization, and the AI drafts trade instructions the client confirms on an IBKR platform. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256.

name: COROS
notes: COROS runs an official remote MCP (workouts, fitness metrics, sleep, HRV) for any COROS account; the endpoint points to the EU host mcpeu.coros.com for sign-in. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256.

name: Remember The Milk
notes: Remember The Milk's official MCP (58 tools, documented for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients) is for Pro members only. Discovery 2026-10-09: no protected-resource metadata; authorization-server metadata at rememberthemilk.com gives DCR yes, CIMD no, S256.

name: pCloud

notes: Official hosted moomoo MCP with OAuth 2.1 (quotes, account and trade scopes incl. trade:write); OpenAPI advertised at no extra charge. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256.

notes: Tiller's MCP reads transactions, balances and holdings in the person's Tiller-powered Google Sheets and edits categories and notes; it needs an active Tiller subscription and is documented for Claude, but any client can use the URL. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256.

notes: Musixmatch runs its own MCP (behind its ChatGPT app; its Claude integration is listed as coming soon) for catalog song search and licensed lyrics, signed in with a Musixmatch account; it does not reach a personal library, and the endpoint is not yet in public docs. name: Photoroom
notes: Official Photoroom MCP edits images through the paid API (about $0.10 per edit, small free allowance) and does not reach saved app designs. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256.

name: Amie
notes: Amie hosts an official remote MCP server for meeting notes, todos, calendar and email; discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, public clients allowed, separate scopes notes:read, todos:read, todos:write, calendar:read, calendar:write, email:read and email:write. Its calendar and email tools reach the person's Gmail, Google Calendar and Outlook accounts through Amie's cloud, so the selected route requests only the notes and todo scopes (Amie's own meeting notes, transcripts, action items and todos) and leaves calendars and mail to the Google Calendar and Outlook plugins; the calendar and email scopes are excluded as proxying other services' data. Amie is paid (Pro or Business after a 7-day trial).

notes: eToro hosts an official MCP server for its Public API, including trade execution; discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256, public clients allowed. The registry entry io.github.gabrielcerutti/etoro-mcp-server is community-built.

name: Habitify
notes: Official Habitify MCP documented for Claude, ChatGPT and any client by URL; reads habits and logs completions. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256 (also plain).

name: Mem
notes: Mem documents its remote MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT and CLIs; free plan has low monthly caps. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, public client (none) allowed.

notes: Roam Research hosts a remote MCP (in Claude's directory as made by Roam Research, at /mcp/claude) that signs in with the person's Roam account and reads and writes the graphs they pick; Roam is a paid subscription. The official local server github.com/Roam-Research/roam-tools is the fallback, using the desktop app's local API and a token. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256 yes.

notes: IDrive runs its own remote MCP with OAuth scopes for drive, backup and sharing; a free basic IDrive plan exists. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256.

Paytm Travel also lists a public flight and bus search MCP (travel.paytm.com/mcp/mcp). Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, PKCE methods not advertised.

name: Luma
notes: Official MCP at https://mcp.luma.com for any Luma account (no Luma Plus needed): event search, the person's events, and hosting tools. Discovery 2026-10-08: authorization server api.luma.com, DCR no, CIMD yes, S256; token auth none, client secret or private_key_jwt.

name: Capacities
notes: Capacities documents its own remote MCP (Streamable HTTP, OAuth with mcp:read and mcp:write). Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256. Whether a paid plan is required for MCP is not stated (the older API Beta page is marked Capacities Pro).

name: Wallet by BudgetBakers
notes: Official remote MCP with OAuth; discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256, public clients. The MCP page does not state a plan requirement, while the REST API is Premium-only.

notes: Official remote MCP (read, search, create and edit cards, journals and whiteboards). Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD not advertised, S256; scopes space:read and space:write. Heptabase itself is a paid subscription after its trial.

name: Manus

notes: MapQuest's remote MCP (geocoding, routing, place search, traffic, static maps) needs a free MapQuest Developer account and key, then OAuth from the agent; it covers location services, not saved places in the consumer app. Discovery 2026-10-09: DCR yes, CIMD no, S256.

notes: Official HIBP MCP (registry io.github.troyhunt/hibp); public breach and Pwned Passwords tools work without sign-in, but email and domain searches need OAuth and an HIBP subscription. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR yes, CIMD yes, S256.
